kaikki_vikisozluk.e: نِينِوَى or نِينَوَى • (nīniwā or nīnawā) f
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Learned borrowing from Akkadian 𒌷𒀏𒆠 (Ninua). The cuneiform sign 𒀏 is formed by a sign denoting a "shrine" (𒀊) with the sign for "fish" (𒄩) inside, a sort of "shrine of the fish", although whether this referred to literal fish, an aspect of Ishtar, a separate Hurrian goddess, or something else entirely is unclear; compare Biblical Hebrew נִינְוֵה (nînəwê)
g: Nineveh (the capital of ancient Assyria, now Mosul, Iraq)
